title: Workload cadence recommender and safe rollforward for coalescing + KV caching
creator: Priya Nair
description:
Problem: Many customer workloads show intermittent microbursts and long-tail sequences where naive coalescing or aggressive KV cache retention reduces token cost but increases tail latency. We need an automated recommender that learns workload cadence (request inter-arrival and sequence length distribution) and produces safe, incremental coalescing + KV caching configs that reduce cost without regressions to p95/p99 latency or QoE.

Goals: 
- Build a workload cadence profiler that classifies workload patterns (steady, bursty, spiky, session-heavy) and extracts key signals: inter-request delta distribution, KV reuse rate, token-length histogram, and sticky-client behaviors.
- Produce a heuristics-driven recommender that maps cadence profiles to an initial config (coalescing window, max microbatch size, KV TTL, prefix cache policy) and a guarded rollout plan.
- Implement a safe rollforward/rollback controller with canary traffic, gradual progression, and automated rollback triggers based on latency, error rate, and quality sampling.
- Surface recommendations in Console with a one-click apply that runs the safe rollout; provide an opt-out and explicit approval flow for Dedicated/Private customers.

Non-goals: global autoscaling policies, model re-quantization, and cross-customer profiling aggregation in this ticket (privacy footprint tracked in separate infra ticket).
acceptance_criteria: Cadence profiler produces stable profile labels for 90% of sampled routes over a 48h window
Recommender outputs initial config with expected cost reduction estimate (token-cost delta) and risk score per route
Safe rollforward controller can run a canary to 5% of traffic, progress to 25%/50%/100% with configurable windows, and auto-rollback on p99 latency increase > 15% or error-rate increase > 0.5%
Console shows recommendation card with estimated savings, risk, and links to telemetry and per-route test traces
End-to-end e2e tests for the canary progression and rollback triggers added to CI
implementation_notes: Profiler: server-side agent will sample request metadata (route, client_id hash, timestamp, tokens_in, tokens_out, KV hit boolean) at 1/1000 sampling for high-volume routes and 1/100 for low-volume routes; aggregated into per-route hour buckets stored in telemetry datastore
Feature extraction: compute inter-arrival percentiles (p10/p50/p90), burst index (p90/p50), session stickiness (unique client_id/session ratio), KV reuse ratio over sliding 1h and 24h windows
Heuristics mapping: map cadence -> preset config templates (conservative/medium/aggressive) and then tune microbatch ceiling by 10/20/30% increments during rollout
Safe controller: leverage rollout service (existing rollout API) to orchestrate canary percentages and watch metric streams from console-traces and cost telemetry

Telemetry: add rollout-specific metrics (canary_p95, canary_p99, canary_error_rate, cost_per_1k_tokens) and a lightweight sampled quality-check pipeline that runs prompt-sets against canary variant and computes surface-level deltas
Privacy: client_id hashed and salted; no raw prompt text stored—quality sampling uses synthetic prompts or anonymized reference prompts per customer consent
updates: 2026-02-12: Kickoff meeting with infra, runtime, and console teams. Agreed scope and non-goals. Assigned Marcus as owner.
2026-02-18: Prototype profiler implemented (sampling + hourly aggregation). Early heatmaps show three dominant cadence classes across customer routes.
2026-02-25: Heuristics draft reviewed with Applied ML; decision to prefer conservative initial configs and rely on gradual percent-based progression to reduce risk.
2026-03-03: Console mockup for recommendation card completed (PM + Design sign-off). Added explicit approval flow for private deployments.
2026-03-06: PoC rollout controller wired to canary metrics stream. First end-to-end shadow apply executed on synthetic workload; observed no regressions but modest savings (4-6%).
2026-03-10: Internal review: Eng lead requested adding p95 watch and a 'quality smoke' step that computes embedding-distance delta on sampled responses before allowing progression beyond 25%.
Next: finish CI e2e tests, add per-route cost projection, and schedule Dedicated customer pilot in Cycle 2026-W11
risks: Aggressive coalescing can increase tail latency for single-request critical flows (payments/auth) — mitigated by route-level allowlist/denylist and traffic class separation
Sampling bias: low-volume routes might be misclassified; we will default to conservative configs and require manual opt-in for aggressive tuning
Quality drift: automated config changes could alter model context behavior; we introduce a sampled quality-check with explicit threshold to block progression
Operational complexity: rollout controller depends on stable metric ingestion; add circuit-breaker to abort progression if telemetry lag > 30s
notes_for_review: Requesting design review on card language: current draft emphasizes 'estimated savings' — PM suggests adding confidence intervals and a 'why we recommend this' bullet
Security: please confirm hashing/salting approach for client_id in telemetry pipeline (cc: security team)
Applied ML: verify KV reuse heuristics and recommend thresholds for TTL tuning
